sections.transcript: Halifax attracts visitors all year round, but since 2010 it is particularly busy in fall when the unique event Halcon takes place. Hal, being short for Halifax, and Khan, short for convention. In Halcon's first year there were 1,700 attendees, a mere six years later an incredible 9,000 delegates crowded into the city for the event. Hal Khan celebrates geek pop culture, a trend that continues to grow in popularity amongst those under 40. To help those unfamiliar with the jargon, we interviewed local organizer Alex Jarvis. He explained that geek pop culture refers to activities of people interested in science fiction, fantasy, video games, board games, comic books, and elaborate role-playing that involves costumes. Jarvis said that many attendees appear in costumes that boggle the mind. These aren't adult versions of Halloween costumes, but clothes carefully crafted by each individual for a unique role-play character. Gaming for these participants means live enactments, not just computer games. Not everyone in the city welcomes such unusual events, perhaps fearing an encounter with an unfamiliar dressed-up character, year. But Halcon will return next year with an expected 10,000 attendees bringing revenue and a dash of colorful excitement.

sections.transcript: In this age of technology, workplace norms and workplace culture are rapidly changing. Previously, employees were generally expected to commute to a physical office and complete their work in company-provided workspaces. Today, with mobile devices such as smartphones, tablets, and laptops being commonplace, many companies are moving towards more flexible work arrangements, with work hours and work locations no longer being fixed. While many welcome such changes, others are not yet convinced. Emmanuel Corley, head of operations at ThinkTech Inc., a global corporation, manages a workforce of 52 employees. Having held this position for over 15 years, Corley takes pride in maintaining a productive and enjoyable work environment. He values teamwork and believes that a productive workplace is is best achieved when co-workers are friends. Consequently, Corley views the growing work from anywhere trend with trepidation. Not only is it more difficult to supervise workers who are not physically present, but with an entire workforce working from home or some other remote location, there is little opportunity for getting to know one's co-workers. Corley worries that while the flexibility of working from anywhere may initially appeal to some, Eventually, employees will feel isolated and lose their sense of commitment. However, for Daniel Sage, a computer programmer, mobile working has had an enormous impact on his ability to maintain a healthy work-life balance. A single father, Sage used to miss countless days of work when his children were homesick. This affected not only his productivity, but also how coworkers and managers perceived his commitment to the company. According to Sage, the stress of trying to keep up with home and work commitments was taking its toll on his health. Having spent the past two years working from home, Sage is emphatic that flexible work arrangements are the way of the future. Although he admits to occasionally missing the camaraderie of his colleagues, the benefits of being able to work when and where he wants far outweigh any drawbacks. attacks. Anita Buffalo, CEO of Global Solutions, acknowledges the concerns of Corley. However, she believes that a mobile workforce can be a win-win situation. Not only do employees appreciate the flexibility and control of order to them, but companies benefit from lower infrastructure costs. If one's entire workforce works from home, the costs involved in maintaining an office space disappear. Although Buffalo admits that switching to mobile work arrangements can pose certain challenges when it comes to employee supervision, she believes that this can be countered by a shift in thinking. At Global Solutions, employee performance is determined solely by the tangible results they achieve, not the time spent in achieving them.

paragraphs: Good afternoon,

I am writing to you regarding the new violin teacher that my daughter has been assigned. My daughter, who is eight years old, has been studying violin at your music school since she was three. As you know, Tara, my daughter's teacher over this five-year span, recently became seriously ill and had to stop teaching. This was a great disappointment to both my daughter and me, as Tara was truly exceptional at her job. We sincerely hope that she recovers soon.

Neither my daughter nor I have been impressed with the teacher chosen to take over Tara's students. At first I thought the problem was one of adjustment and that it would resolve itself once the teacher was used to the new school and students. However, after 2 months, nothing has improved, and I have come to realize that the teacher is simply unprofessional and poorly qualified. She has been late for almost every one of my daughter's lessons. While I can understand occasionally being held up in traffic, this problem has become habitual. Since my daughter's lessons are only 30 minutes long, the 5 to 10 minutes she loses each week due to her teacher's tardiness are significant. Furthermore, I seriously question whether this teacher should be teaching young children. She has very little patience and frequently loses her temper when my daughter makes a mistake. In addition, my daughter is sent home from each lesson with more pieces than any 8-year-old should be expected to learn in a week. Music is supposed to be her hobby, not her job.

Since beginning with this new teacher, I have noticed both my daughter's confidence and interest in playing the violin have declined significantly, a fact which likely led to the lower-than-usual mark she received on her recent music exam. Therefore, effective immediately, I would ask you to assign her to an alternate instructor. I have been very impressed with your school until now, but if you are unable to find a suitable replacement for this teacher, I will have no other choice but to cancel all of my daughter's future lessons.
Sincerely,
Mario Perez

paragraphs: A. One of the most popular tourist attractions of the Maritime Provinces is Green Gables House in Prince Edward Island. Of course, Anne herself is a fictional character in the novels of Lucy Maud Montgomery. However, the places Anne supposedly inhabited, especially the Green Gables farmhouse, attract many thousands of tourists every year. Shopkeepers market items based on the novels, even straw hats with red braids so that young girls can look like Anne. She is also celebrated in a permanently running live musical in the capital city of Charlottetown.

B. Anne and her story have attracted Canadian fans since 1908. The dated language and Anne's enthusiastic monologues of the original text are challenging to read, but once you meet Anne Shirley, rescued from an orphanage by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, you are hooked into her life. Anne's story is based on Montgomery's own life. Born in a PEI village, Montgomery was an orphan by age seven and raised by her strict, Cuthbert-like grandparents in Cavendish. Montgomery had a lonely childhood and depended on imaginary friends, just like Anne did. Like Anne, Montgomery was lively, intelligent, and flirtatious, and, like Anne, she supported herself as a teacher.

C. Montgomery wrote six novels about Anne, portraying her life from age 11 to 40. The first book, Anne of Green Gables, appeals to women of all ages. Many readers have tried to analyze this appeal, which boils down to this: Anne shows us the key to essential happiness. She represents all women, especially during the formative years, wanting to be smart, funny, honest, and optimistic. Anne agonized over her red hair, frequently a stigma that invites teasing. All women may not worry about red hair, but all worry about their faults and their looks, especially at Anne's age in the first book.

D. The Anne books, translated into more than 30 languages, attract readers worldwide. The Japanese are among the most ardent of Anne fans, often flying more than 10,000 kilometers for 18 hours to spend a few days visiting Anne sites in PEI. Japanese is spoken at most of the tourist attractions and shops in PEI. Anne even attracted the attention of Prince William and his bride Kate Middleton during their visit to Canada in 2011. Anne of Green Gables was the Duchess's favourite book as a child, so she made sure their tour included PEI. Like most Anne enthusiasts, Kate yearned to see Anne's homeland.
E. Not given in any of the above paragraphs.

paragraphs: A recent surge of high-profile data breaches has prompted renewed interest in cybersecurity. At issue is the security and confidentiality of thousands of terabytes of business and government data. Some experts are now warning that, unless drastic steps are taken to strengthen cybersecurity, the entire process of digitalization could be threatened.

The past few months have been really unnerving for a lot of decision-makers. People read the news and they realize that breaches could happen to their company, often jeopardizing years of work, if not their organization's very survival," said Mona Jackman, a federal government policy analyst. "It's gotten to the point where people are questioning the whole digital revolution. I can't really say I blame them. When you look at the scale of the leaks and the strength of the organizations that were hacked, you have to feel vulnerable. If you are a small business owner who depends on proprietary information, isn't it better to leave everything offline and stick with pen and paper methods?

Those who say that hacking could somehow harm the IT industry don't understand the long-term technological forces that are at work. Solutions are being found as more cash is infused into the system," opined Cassandra Black, an IT industry analyst. "Security consultants make thousands of dollars installing firewalls, authentication software, and cyberactivity monitoring systems. Cybersecurity companies have been flourishing; these high-profile hacking cases are like free publicity for them.

However, not everyone believes that more costly, sophisticated systems are the answer to modern cybersecurity threats. "When dealing with hackers, the best tool we have in our arsenal is education," weighs in Mark Levinstein, Chief Information Officer at a large Canadian engineering consulting firm. "Most of these large leaks were the results of very simple phishing scams, whereby hackers were unwittingly given network access by employees. I don't worry for the IT industry, because these are basic issues that can be resolved at a low cost, but we need proper training and coordination across the sector.

Talk to John's mother. Explain why she should let John go to the music festival.
